Metro paramedics under seige

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Friday night with the Paramedics

Unique Selling Point:
In a desperate moment of need at the scene of an accident, a heart attack, or other medical emergencies we call the Metro paramedics, depending on them to arrive as quickly as possible. But more and more these angels of mercy are being attacked while they deliver their life saving services. We ride along on a routine Friday night speaking to them about their fears, the attacks they have endured and what they want to be put in place to ensure their safety.

Summary:
There have been over 100 attacks on Metro paramedics in the Western Cape since January 2016, there have been 7 attacks since January. It’s a growing phenomenon which is happening all over the country. Metro workers are unarmed without any protective clothing, and these opportunistic attacks are not only for their personal belongings like cellphones and wallets, but also for the equipment and pharmaceuticals in the ambulance. These people are risking their lives to save people they don’t even know and when they set off for a weekend shift, they do so with increasing fear.
In some areas where gang wars are common like Hanover Park, Langa and Manenberg, Metro ambulance staff have to wait for a police escort before responding to a call. This delayed response time is also impacting other patients in “safe” areas because of the longer turnaround time in responding to the “hot spots”
The insert will accompany Metro workers on a Friday evening, interviewing them about how they feel, what has happened to them and how they think their situation could be improved, as well as filming the situations they are responding to while protecting the identity of the patients if needs be.

Press Release:


EMS Paramedics
They’re usually the first respondents at the scene of an accident or a medical emergency, but in recent months, paramedics have endured knife attacks,
beatings and robberies while on duty. Unarmed and without protective gear, they remain vulnerable to being attacked by opportunists. Why are these angels
of mercy under siege? Carte Blanche investigates.

Script:


Damien 06 18 15 13 I have been gun pointed 5 times within my own community and its crazy and its heinous its evil in fact that the community isn’t siding with us
Script: Across the country Paramedics are increasingly coming under attack- they have been shot at, beaten, stabbed and raped while out attending to patients.
Damien 06 18 16 the police at time tell us listen one police van cannot enter an area they need to wait for backup I am here with an ambulance, all that I have is medical equipment, these people are armed and these people are afraid to enter the area what does that tell you
Script: Damien Allen and his partner Rushana Gallow have been robbed numerous times and caught in gang crossfire
Rushana 00 39 30 18 the bullet came through the windscreen but I kind of ducked down so it got my arm. If I never ducked down it probably would have hit my head or my chest so after that I kind of freaked me out
Script: In the Western Cape there have already been 8 attacks on Paramedics this year. Cecily Marais and Bonginkosi Lawulake are the most recent victims
Cecily “The patient was already in the ambulance when we got attacked
Script: It was early Saturday evening when they set off for Tafelsig in Mitchells Plain, hoping the police escort would offer some protection from the drunk crowd
Cecily 01 15 12 30 her mother was the one who decided she wanted to come with but she would not leave the patient alone or allow me to start looking at her… she started shoving me and then when she missed shoving me she hit me on the jaw, it was very painful
Bonginkosi 0116 41 16 the way that mama was fighting her it was terrible and then I quickly run and when I try to open the door I feel the impact of the fist here and I don’t know how and where… It was the lady telling us we are useless and she tried again to hit me
Script: The tension in the air as South Metro prepares for their night shift is quite palpable. The evening briefing takes on an ominous tone as District manager Jakob Van Zyl urges them not to take unnecessary risks, they are unarmed and don’t have bullet proof vest
JA 05 39 11 24 ….we do not want to encourage people to attack us to rob therefore we have no protection. There is a total disregard of law enforcement
Script: Having heard the horror stories, we wanted to see first-hand what a night shift on the Cape Flats involved, Zenade Morrow and Berenice Fillis took us along
John “So tell us about the area we are going to now
Zenade Morrow “We received a call we are on our way to Browns Farm Philippi it is classified as one of our red areas the main concerns we have here is lighting we are unable to see what is going on its quite dark and people are popping out everywhere you are hearing voices but I don’t see people so at the end of the day we have to be vigilant
Script: The Philippi police station situated under the railway bridge is extremely dark
Zenade” ….. the problem is now we just have to pray there is a van available
Link 06 47 25 18 So this is the procedure every time an ambulance moves into a red zone they have to stop off at a police station and arrange an escort and the real sadness is that somewhere out there, there is a one year old child in need of medical attention
Script: They are sitting ducks as they wait outside, often for several hours. They been robbed numerous times waiting for an escort
Zenade Morrow ‘ ja we have SAPS escort we are on our way just inform them to get ready
John 06 49 48 10 so you are familiar with the area we are going to it’s got a bit of a track record
Zenade Morrow “Ja a few months ago one of our crew was actually attacked in this area where we are going to where both were almost assaulted but managed to get away quite severe damage also done to the vehicle where a group of guys tried to attack them
De Vries 04 52 31 17 My staff go in there with gloves and a red light. How do I protect my staff how do we as the Departments management protect them when we know the job is inherently unsafe
Script: Dr Shaheem De Vries Provincial Director of EMS, says the psychological stress of the job is taking its toll , they have lost 50 000 hours to staff on sick leave. It’s pushing up the overtime costs and adding to the load for those on duty
John” How often are the attacks happening?
De Vries 04 50 46 11 there is an average of between 4 and 6 a month and they vary from an ambulance being stoned and they progress into acts of physical violence threats and the extreme of end my staff are beaten or held up at gun point
Script: Sometimes Paramedics get called out on fake emergencies into deserted dark places and ambushed. Nopasika Ponso and her partner initially thought the two men that approached the ambulance were the patient’s relatives - till they saw the guns
Nopasika 00 03 39 13 I didn’t think he would smash the glass with the gun but he did and immediately all the doors opened and then he came straight to me pointing at me on the forehead with a gun demanding stuff- he became so violent
Script: Then they started to drag Nopasika out of the ambulance to rape her
Nopasika 00 05 22 20 then they pulled me but after some time they just left they just ran away I don’t know why then after that I collapsed
Script: Every attack leaves them traumatised, and an already over stretched ambulance service loses a crew for a few days or sometimes months
Cecily 01 21 31 09 this is a family member I am supposed to be safe with the patient’s own family and they hurt me so anybody can hurt me and that has an impact. 01 19 56 09 I think through the years I have had so many incidences and stuff it is almost like I have an ongoing post- traumatic stress..I am medicated for stress
Rushana 06 14 47 06 the palpitations the fear of something happening it is always going to be there- not just with us I honestly believe everybody feels that way – we are all scared
Link 06 52 21 22 Once in the red zone the idea is to do what is know as a load and go that is to get the patient into the ambulance and leave
Script: This time it was a quick exist because the mother could carry the baby. But often it’s a slow process and while they focus on the patient they are vulnerable.
This hit and run victim had to be removed from the red zone and once they retreated to a safe area they could stabilise him, potentially lifesaving moments are lost but they have no choice
De Vries 04 54 06 21 these communities are the very same communities are the very same communities that suffer every day under the very violence that now directed at us so it is a double injury if we were now to say it is so violent in your area we aren’t going to service those areas
Link 06 57 39 02 Many of the provinces ambulances are fitted with tablets like this one it makes the job incredibly efficient the trouble is that these are on the criminals shopping list
Script: Crews are attacked for their personal belongings like wallets and cells phones - they are crimes of opportunity. Sihle Ndunge was taking her patients vital signs when suddenly the ambulance door was ripped open and she was kicked to the floor hitting her head
Sihle “ He stabbed me on the arm because he wanted the phone and then he strangled me and then when he was strangling me that is when he opened my pockets to get the money that I had
Script: Only when the thugs in the front managed to rip out the computer did he stop assaulting her
Sihle 00 29 39 09 I am frightened every time I get a call to do a house call … I am scared of them I am scared of everyone at the moment
Link: 05 34 21 21 Cape Town’s ambulance teams try to respond to calls within about 15 minutes but with the additional security that is required when moving into the so called red zones that figure can sometimes climb to around several hours and of course as a result of that it has a knock on effect in other parts of the city
Script: There only between 60 and 70 metro ambulances in Cape Town and so areas that can be accessed quickly are waiting longer for help because ambulances are tied up in the red zones
Cecily 01 30 56 ……it has happened before that patients have died because of the delay they are angry they do get upset they do get aggressive and I think it’s understandable
John 06 33 50 14 Doesn’t it exhaust you having to work under those conditions
Berenice Fillis “Yes it does because we all have families at home and you want to return to them whole I mean even when we don’t get injured physically but emotionally and injury to one of us is an injury to all because it effects everyone
Rushana 06 17 My parents, I still live with them, and they have asked me multiple times after each incident to find something else because they freak out and they stress whenever we working
Sheldon 07 46 35 00 I don’t tell my wife about all the times that I go in and I know she worries about it and I know she doesn’t sleep very well when I am on night shift
Script: ER24 assist metro when they have an emergency. Sheldon Poisson and his partner Grant Josephs were attending to a seriously ill child in Khayalisha when they had a gun put to their heads
Grant 07 42 24 00 Ja I looked down the barrel , and I just turned around and I just kept on treating my patient …and I just thought to myself whatever happens happens
John 07 50 48 16 and this was happening while you the child was having seizures
Sheldon 07 41 27 18 That was the part that really amazed me, the fact that they could see the child was in distress and we were trying to help the child and their concern was what can I get from you
Script: Paramedics are desperate – the police often have to leave them at the scene to attend to a crime
Damien 06 16 24 12 people doing the bread in the morning those people have armed guards guarding those trucks for bread so why can’t it be done for us why can’t we have some sort of service or private security escorting us into those areas
Script: MEC for Community Safety Dan Plato says he’s aware police escorts aren’t ideal. He’s next plan is safety kiosks with private security and neighbourhood watches in dangerous areas
Dan Plato 07 15 03 21 Ambulance personnel report to that base, pick-up the security personnel, drive with the security personnel to the address of the patient , drive back to the base drop off the security personnel
Script: And it’s can’t come soon enough. What struck us about all these Paramedics was how brave and passionate they continue to be despite the circumstances
Nopasika 00 17 04 21 if I resign I am letting these culprits win they are winning it’s like I am defeated
Cecily 01 31 23 07 this is my passion this is my job

This delayed response time is also impacting other patients in “safe” areas because of the longer turnaround time in responding to the “hot spots” The insert will accompany Metro workers on a Friday evening, interviewing them about how they feel, what has happened to them and how they think their situation could be improved, as well as filming the situations they are responding to while protecting the identity of the patients if needs be.
